title: Anand Rathi AM interview
source: Anand Rathi Wealth Account Manager revision guide, company profile and wealth management interview prep notes
purpose: Preparing for an Account Manager (wealth management) interview at Anand Rathi Wealth.
about: Company facts, tax, return and risk formulas, fund selection, operations, products and client scenarios. Tax rates as of FY2025-26; confirm live rates.

sections.title: Anand Rathi Wealth and the role
sections.why: "What do you know about us?" and "why this role?" come first in almost every interview.

questions.prompt: Since when has Anand Rathi run its private wealth business?
questions.hint: The Group is older than the wealth business.
questions.answer: Group founded **1994**; private wealth since **2002**; Rawal CEO since 2007; listed 2021.

questions.prompt: Who serves as Anand Rathi Wealth's Joint CEO?
questions.hint: Joined in 2012, Joint CEO from April 2025.
questions.answer: **Feroze Azeez**, Joint CEO from 10 Apr 2025. **Rakesh Rawal** is Executive Director and CEO since 2007.

questions.prompt: Roughly how big is Anand Rathi Wealth (30 Sep 2026)?
options: AUM above ₹5 lakh cr; 1 lakh families
questions.answer: **₹1,08,377 cr+ AUM, 14,309+ client families.** ₹37,900 cr is the market cap, not AUM.

questions.prompt: When did Anand Rathi Wealth list, and at what IPO price?
questions.hint: The issue price is the lower of the two numbers.
questions.answer: IPO **₹550**, NSE listing **₹600**, a ~9.09% gain. Bonus shares mean today's price isn't comparable.

questions.prompt: Which listing-gain calculation is right?
questions.hint: Gain is measured against the issue price.
questions.answer: Gain over the **issue price**: 50/550 ≈ 9.09%.

questions.prompt: The JD stresses one idea twice. Which should you echo?
questions.hint: What sets the firm apart from a distributor?
options: Advisory against a plan, not product selling
questions.answer: Use **advisory, not product selling** in your why-us answer.

questions.prompt: What is the Account Manager role at its core?
questions.hint: Who does the AM work alongside?
options: Supporting an RM: plans, reports, documents, queries
Running a fund as portfolio manager
Selling products to new walk-in clients alone
questions.answer: An **RM-support** role: planning and reporting, spotting opportunities, BD, documentation and client queries.

questions.prompt: Asked about structured products, your gap, you should…
options: Say you've studied payoff, issuer and liquidity, not executed
Claim you've sold many to HNIs
Say they're outside an AM's job
Change the subject to mutual funds
questions.answer: Don't bluff: "I've studied the payoff, issuer and liquidity logic but not executed these."

sections.title: Taxation
sections.why: Tax-aware advice is in your pitch, so expect a worked tax question.

questions.prompt: Equity fund units held over 12 months are taxed at…
options: 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year
10% on gains above ₹1 lakh a year
questions.answer: Equity LTCG: **12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh**. Short-term (under 12 months): **20%**. Plus 4% cess.

questions.prompt: Debt fund (over 65% debt) gains held 3 years are taxed at…
options: Your slab rate, whatever the holding period
questions.answer: 'Specified' debt funds: **slab rate**, no LTCG benefit, any holding period.

questions.prompt: When units are redeemed, which lots go first?
questions.answer: **FIFO**: first in, first out. That's why you check tax lot by lot before a rebalance.

questions.prompt: Equity fund: ₹20 L grows to ₹26 L in 18 months. Tax before cess?
questions.answer: Held over 12 months → LTCG. Taxable ₹4,75,000 × 12.5% = **₹59,375**; with 4% cess ₹61,750.

questions.prompt: 30% slab client, 1-year+ parking. Why arbitrage over liquid?
options: Equity taxation: LTCG 12.5% above ₹1.25 L vs slab
Arbitrage has no exit load ever
Liquid funds can't be held over a year
questions.answer: Pre-tax returns are similar, but arbitrage gets **equity taxation**. Under a year it's 20% STCG; and it can dip slightly.

questions.prompt: How can a long-term capital loss be set off?
questions.hint: It's the narrower of the two rules.
questions.answer: LTCL → **LTCG only**. STCL → either. Carry forward **8 years**.

questions.prompt: What does grandfathering do for equity bought before 1 Feb 2018?
options: Cost = higher of actual cost and 31 Jan 2018 value
Gains before 2018 are fully tax-free forever
Pre-2018 units are taxed at slab
questions.answer: Cost is lifted to the **higher of actual cost and 31 Jan 2018 value** (capped at sale value).

questions.prompt: IDCW (dividend) payouts from a fund are taxed…
questions.hint: It's income, not a capital gain.
options: At slab; TDS 10% above ₹10,000 a year
questions.answer: IDCW is **slab-taxed**, TDS 10% above ₹10,000. NAV falls by the payout, so it isn't extra return.

questions.prompt: A switch between two schemes of the same AMC is…
questions.hint: What happens to the old units?
options: A redemption plus purchase, so taxable
Tax-free as it stays in one AMC
Taxed only on the new scheme
questions.answer: A switch is a **sale + buy**: check tax, exit load and NAV cut-off.

sections.title: Return and risk formulas
sections.why: Reporting (IRR/XIRR, variance vs plan) is core to the job; expect at least one formula.

questions.prompt: Which is the CAGR formula?
A 20% absolute return over 2 years, annualised, is…
questions.answer: Annualise by compounding: 1.20^(1/2) − 1 ≈ **9.54%**.

questions.prompt: Monthly SIPs plus a withdrawal. Which return measure fits?
questions.answer: **XIRR**: the rate where NPV of all dated flows = 0. CAGR fits one lump sum and two dates.

questions.prompt: Why can a report's return differ from the client's IRR?
questions.hint: One strips out the client's timing.
options: TWR ignores flow timing; IRR is money-weighted
They can never differ on one portfolio
questions.answer: **TWR** judges the manager; **IRR/XIRR** reflects the client's actual flows. Money added before a fall hurts IRR.

questions.prompt: Which is the Sharpe ratio?
questions.hint: Excess return per unit of total risk.
questions.answer: Sharpe = (Rp − Rf)/σp. (12 − 6)/10 = **0.60**. Divide by β for Treynor, downside dev. for Sortino.

questions.prompt: How does Sortino differ from Sharpe?
options: Uses the benchmark instead of Rf
questions.answer: **Sortino** penalises only downside volatility: (Rp − Rf)/downside dev.

questions.prompt: Which is Jensen's alpha?
Which is the information ratio?
questions.hint: Active return per unit of active risk.

questions.prompt: Beta 1.2, market up 10%. The fund is likely to move…
questions.hint: Beta is sensitivity, not a promise.
questions.answer: Beta = Cov(Rp, Rm)/Var(Rm). 1.2 × 10% ≈ **+12%**, not guaranteed.

questions.prompt: A portfolio falls from ₹10 L to ₹8 L. Max drawdown is…
questions.hint: Peak to trough, over the peak.
questions.answer: Max drawdown = (Trough − Peak)/Peak = **−20%**. Good for explaining possible pain to a client.

sections.title: Fund selection and capture ratios
sections.why: You cite capture ratios and fund categories as your Dezerv strengths, so they'll probe.

questions.prompt: Benchmark averages +4% in up months, fund +3.6%. Upside capture?
questions.answer: Upside capture = fund's avg up-month return ÷ benchmark's × 100 = **90%**.

questions.prompt: Upside 90, downside 70. What's the capture ratio and reading?
questions.answer: Above 1 means it gives up less on falls than it gains on rises.

questions.prompt: Which capture profile is the worst?
questions.answer: Lags in rallies **and** falls more in corrections. Both below 100 is defensive; both above is aggressive.

questions.prompt: Caveats when using capture ratios? Pick all that apply.
options: Higher upside always means a better fund
questions.answer: A few months can drive the ratio. Same benchmark, same category, rolling windows, plus other risk measures.

questions.prompt: Large cap vs multi cap: what's the SEBI rule?
options: Large ≥80% top 100; multi ≥25% each in large, mid, small
Large ≥65% top 100; multi ≥65% in any cap
Large ≥80% top 250; multi ≥35% large and mid
questions.answer: Mid cap ≥65% in 101–250; small ≥65% in 251+; flexi ≥65% equity, any cap (manager's choice).

questions.prompt: Which category must hold ≥10% in each of 3+ asset classes?
questions.answer: Multi-asset: e.g. equity, debt, gold. **Multi cap** is about market caps, not asset classes.

questions.prompt: Direct vs regular plan of the same fund differ in…
options: Expense ratio: regular pays distributor commission
questions.answer: Same holdings; **regular** carries commission in a higher expense ratio. Advice must be worth the gap.

questions.prompt: Two funds show the same return. You recommend…
options: The one with better risk-adjusted fit for the client
The one with the bigger AUM
questions.answer: Compare volatility, Sharpe/Sortino, drawdown, capture, concentration, cost and consistency, then fit to the client.

sections.title: Operations: KYC, CAS, folios, AA
sections.why: Documentation and client queries are a big share of the AM's week.

questions.prompt: Depository CAS vs RTA CAS: what does each cover?
options: NSDL/CDSL: demat holdings; CAMS/KFin: MF folios
NSDL/CDSL: MF folios; CAMS/KFin: demat shares
RTA CAS covers bank accounts too
questions.answer: A client holding both forms needs **both** statements to see everything.

questions.prompt: What is a folio?
options: An investor's account number with an AMC; many schemes can sit in it
A demat account with a DP
questions.answer: Holding patterns: single, joint, either-or-survivor. Non-demat units live in the folio.

questions.prompt: Which two are RTAs?
questions.answer: NSDL/CDSL are depositories; CRISIL/ICRA are rating agencies; NSE/BSE are exchanges.

questions.prompt: Who regulates the Account Aggregator framework?
questions.answer: AAs are **RBI-regulated NBFC-AAs**. SEBI covers MFs, brokers, RIAs, PMS, AIFs, REITs/InvITs.

questions.prompt: True of Account Aggregators? Pick all that apply.
options: Fetches holdings without PDFs or passwords
The AA stores and analyses your data
questions.answer: FIPs (banks, RTAs, depositories) share with FIUs (advisers) through the AA, encrypted.

questions.prompt: A client's KYC shows 'on hold' at the KRA. What happens?
options: Transactions are blocked until it's fixed
questions.answer: KYC status controls whether you can transact. Missing FATCA, nomination, mobile or email can freeze a folio too.

questions.prompt: Distributor vs RIA: how is each paid?
options: Distributor: product commission; RIA: client fee
Both paid only by the client
questions.answer: Distributors hold an **ARN** (AMFI); RIAs are SEBI-registered, fee-based fiduciaries. Don't guess Anand Rathi's category.

questions.prompt: Bank mandate change: what do you collect?
options: RTA form + cancelled cheque or statement + KYC
Only a phone call from the client
questions.answer: The RTA processes it; some AMCs apply a short cooling period on redemptions to a new account.

sections.title: Bonds, REITs, structured products
sections.why: The JD lists bonds, structured products and alternatives as opportunities you'll spot.

questions.prompt: Modified duration 4, yields rise 1%. Price moves about…
questions.answer: Rates up, prices down; longer bonds fall more.

questions.prompt: Which is current yield?
questions.hint: Uses today's price, not face value.
questions.answer: Coupon/face is the coupon rate. **YTM** also uses redemption value and time.

questions.prompt: Dirty price equals…
questions.answer: Buyers pay the **dirty** price; quotes are usually clean.

questions.prompt: REITs and InvITs must distribute at least…
questions.answer: Also: net debt capped at **49%** (above 25% needs AAA and unitholder approval); REITs ≥80% in completed assets.

questions.prompt: G-sec yields rise. REIT unit prices tend to…
questions.answer: REITs behave partly like bonds. Yield isn't guaranteed: it depends on rentals and leverage.

questions.prompt: A 'principal-protected' note is usually built from…
options: A zero-coupon bond plus an index option
An equity fund plus an FD
A gilt fund plus a REIT
A liquid fund plus a futures short
questions.answer: Protection holds **only at maturity and only if the issuer pays**. Upside is partial and may be capped.

questions.prompt: What's the core risk in a principal-protected MLD?
questions.answer: Even if the index rises, an issuer default loses principal. Also illiquidity, lock-in, slab tax.

questions.prompt: PMS vs AIF minimum ticket?
questions.answer: PMS holds securities in your demat, taxed per trade. AIF Cat I/II mostly pass-through; Cat III taxed at fund level.

sections.title: Client scenarios
sections.why: Clients are 45–60 and very wealthy; they'll test judgement and calm.

questions.prompt: Client wants 15% a year with zero risk. You…
options: Say no such product exists; ask goals; show trade-offs
Recommend small caps for the return
questions.answer: Be honest that return needs risk, then split safe money for known needs and growth money for long goals.

questions.prompt: Equity is 68% against a 60% target. The variance is…
options: +8 pts: a prompt to review, not an automatic sale
questions.answer: Rebalance using fresh money and SIPs first, then redemptions; check tax, exit loads and costs.

questions.prompt: House view shifts equity to debt. Across 50 clients you…
options: Rank clients by deviation; give the RM an action list with tax
Switch every client the same day
questions.answer: Compare each against plan and tactical band, check tax, exit costs and goal timing, then track execution.

questions.prompt: Portfolio down 12%, client angry. First step?
options: Listen and acknowledge, then check against benchmark
Blame the market and move on
questions.answer: Then: market-wide or specific? Still on plan? Horizon and liquidity? The RM leads with your analysis.

questions.prompt: 55-year-old fears a correction. Your best reassurance?
questions.hint: Where do the next few years' needs sit?
options: Next 3–5 years of needs are in debt and liquid
Equity always recovers within a year
Time the market with a stop-loss
questions.answer: Equity is for goals 7+ years away, so a fall doesn't force a sale. Phase new money; don't time the market.

questions.prompt: Product team pushes an SP you think is unsuitable. You…
options: Document why, raise with RM/compliance, offer an alternative
Sell it with a quiet disclaimer
questions.answer: Mis-selling harms the client and the firm.

questions.prompt: You spot a documentation error after a transaction. You…
options: Escalate now, try to fix before cut-off, tell the client
Wait to see if the client notices
Reverse the trade without telling anyone
questions.answer: Then log it and add a process check so it doesn't repeat.

questions.prompt: Risk profiling: tolerance and capacity differ. Plan to…
questions.answer: Tolerance = willingness; capacity = ability. Add horizon, liquidity needs and experience.
